cases.title: A returning learner picks up what was still wrong

rubric.reason: read_learner_record ran before snapshot_project, and the opening says in plain words 'Four days ago you eased the Title's Position... Scale and Opacity were the two still moving at a constant speed, and they still are, so let's finish those,' which picks up the record's still-wrong pairs without naming the file or its fields.

Every name the mentor uses (Title, Subtitle, CTRL, Bar, Glow, Old Take, Icon, Mentor Practice, Scale and Opacity at 0.5 s → 1.5 s) matches the snapshot_project result; Title › Position comes from the read_learner_record result and is absent from the snapshot's linear findings, so 'still eased' matches.

The mentor called read_learner_record before snapshot_project, and its opening recalls the earlier lesson in plain words ("Last Thursday you eased Title's Position… Scale and Opacity were the two still linear, and they still are"). The proposal picks up the practicing skill's unfinished pairs, and it mentions no file or field names.

Every name and time in the reply matches a tool result: Title › Scale and Title › Opacity at 0.5–1.5 s, Old Take as hidden, Icon as a precomp, Mentor Practice, and "9 linear pairs on 6 layers" all come from snapshot_project, and Title's Position comes from the learner record result.

read_learner_record ran before snapshot_project, and the opening says in plain words 'you eased Title's Position… Scale and Opacity were still linear, and they still are', then proposes picking up Title › Scale and Opacity (0.5 s → 1.5 s), which matches the record's next step and the snapshot, without naming the file or its fields.

Every name and time mentioned matches a tool result: Title › Scale and Opacity at 0.5–1.5 s, Old Take (hidden_layers), Icon (precomp_layers) and Mentor Practice come from snapshot_project, Title's Position comes from the learner record, and '9 linear pairs on 6 layers' matches counts.linear and the six layers in findings.
